outcome_detail: $300,000 settlement; Spokane City Council unanimously approved it in March 2024 (reported March 25, 2024), resolving a $1 million claim filed against the city in 2022.
criminal_detail: Former officer Nathan Nash was convicted by a Spokane jury in September 2022 of third-degree rape in this plaintiff's case and second-degree rape with aggravating circumstances against a second woman, both committed on duty in 2019. In October 2022 he was sentenced to 14 years to life in prison; he has been appealing.
description: A woman filed a $1 million claim against the City of Spokane in 2022, alleging the police department ignored red flags about officer Nathan Nash's behavior before he raped her and another woman in 2019 during follow-up visits to assault investigations he had responded to on duty. Nash was convicted by a jury in September 2022 of third-degree rape in her case and of second-degree rape with aggravating circumstances against the second woman, and was sentenced in October 2022 to 14 years to life in prison. In March 2024, the Spokane City Council unanimously approved a $300,000 settlement of her claim. The second woman's separate case against the city settled for $400,000 in 2025 (see companion record), bringing the city's total payouts tied to Nash's 2019 conduct to $700,000.
notes: Companion record rec-46b covers the second woman's separate $400,000 settlement with the city over Nash's 2019 conduct.
